needs.reason: Projects, their folders, dependsOn and the versions are literal in build.sbt and project/. Only sbt, which compiles build.sbt and project/*.sbt as Scala, gives the evaluated settings: the cross-versioned artifact names, the implicit scala3-library dependency and the default source directories.

traps: The three sbt projects are all declared in one file, build.sbt; core and app have no manifest of their own. The unit names are the lazy val ids (root, core, app); ledger, ledger-core and ledger-app are the artifact names set by name :=.
%% appends the Scala binary version: cats-core becomes the artifact cats-core_3, scalatest becomes scalatest_3. A text reader that keeps the written name cats-core misses the artifact.
ThisBuild / scalaVersion sets Scala 3.3.4 for all three projects; sbt downloads that compiler and adds org.scala-lang:scala3-library_3:3.3.4 to each project without any line naming it.
app gets cats-core only transitively through dependsOn(core); it declares no library.
aggregate(core, app) makes root run the tasks of both but is not a classpath dependency: root depends_on nothing.
project/ is the meta-build, itself an sbt build compiled with Scala 2.12: project/plugins.sbt adds sbt-scalafmt (artifact sbt-scalafmt_2.12_1.0) and project/build.properties pins sbt 1.10.5.
project/build.properties has no comment line, so Linguist classifies it as INI, not Java Properties.
The scalafmt version 3.8.3 in .scalafmt.conf is downloaded by the plugin at format time; it is neither a toolchain nor a declared dependency.
Java has no version anywhere: sbt runs on whatever JDK is installed.
root is the aggregating project at the workspace root; the members are core and app.
